reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens: refuted. The expected public gain is well below +0.002, and the one new element (flow-compensated midpoint) already failed in our own lab. (1) ARITHMETIC. Public J_div 0.36 (CONTEXT L1319-1320) gives a break-even fork precision of 0.265. With the assumed public TP19/FP13/FN21 (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.notes.md), I recomputed with J=(TP+t)/(TP+FP+FN+f), 0.1 weight. For 7 extra evaluable forks: precision 0.20 gives -0.0010; 0.27 gives +0.0001; 0.30 gives +0.0006; 0.40 gives +0.0023; 0.50 gives +0.0040. With 15 forks: 0.20 gives -0.0020, 0.40 gives +0.0045. So +0.002 needs MARGINAL precision >= ~0.40. Why 7 forks: the lab analogue added 15 evaluable forks on ~88 CONFIRMATION GT divisions, which scales to about 7 on ~40 public ones. The best marginal steal precision we have ever measured is 0.27 (4/15), from a TRAINED DaughterNet (AUC 0.875; CONTEXT L1300-1310), and that gave LB +0.001. (2) The mechanism has less discriminating power than claimed. (a) Our own lab already tested velocity-compensated midpoints (div_audit9, wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.notes.md). They were WORSE than plain midpoints (TP max 4.4 um, 3 TP >= 4 um), and half-velocity was no better than plain. (b) Forum base rates (browser_research_2026-09-24.md L94, discussion 740573): on contested links, velocity extrapolation picks the true child 0 of 381 times. Steals are exactly contested links. (c) Plain midpoint separation between TP and FP forks is weak: medians 1.58 vs 3.02 um, and on GT divisions median 2.33, p90 5.24. The hard gates (both steps 2-7 um, cos <= -0.25) already force the gated candidates' midpoints close to s, so the midpoint term adds little on top of the gates. (3) Prior and reach. B32 steal pool: 97 positives in 16.3M triples, about 1:170k (b32_step1_candidate_audit.md). My guessed estimate from the GT base rates in CONTEXT L733-736: the proposed gates keep about 45% of real divisions (division step p75 7.36 um, so both steps <= 7 in about 60%; sister 5-14 um in about 85%; cos gate about 80%). That leaves about 17 of the 39 steal-type GT divisions on 199 videos, against a prior still around 1:10^4. A geometric score with a likelihood ratio of about 2-3 cannot lift that to precision 0.3-0.4. The lab ceiling at precision 1 is +0.009, and a realistic lab result (+5 TP / +15-25 FP) is +0.0009 to +0.0015. That result is also in-sample, because detector positions and the DeepCenter veto are trained on these videos. (4) Transfer. Positions come from the in-sample detector plus the V1284 head. The head was trained on ~20 train videos, and its 199-video retrain learned 6bba's z offset. The midpoint and sister terms are dominated by z, the worst axis out of sample, so precision on unseen embryos can only drop. The public embryo is division-easy (J 0.36 vs lab 0.12), so it punishes low-precision forks most. The private embryos may be lab-like (break-even ~0.11-0.2), so a small private gain is possible, but that is not observable. (5) Interaction risks. The pass competes with the #35 DaughterNet steal insertion for the same forks. Forks made inside the relink run BEFORE safe-div, so under the frame caps in dense frames they can displace safe-div forks, which have higher precision (lab 0.35, public est. ~0.6). Steal-with-repair also turns correct annotated neighbour continuations into 1 FN + 2 FP edges. (6) Validation. The H3 head-coordinate lab does not exist yet, and the exp39 fallback has no head coordinates, so the claimed premise cannot be tested before the probe. Its own gate (added-fork precision >= 0.31 on each embryo) is one that the trained DaughterNet already failed (0.27).
fix_if_any: No repair gets this to +0.002 public by geometry alone. Salvage options, in order: (a) Do NOT spend an LB slot on it standalone. (b) If #35 (DaughterNet insertion) wins, reuse only the CANDIDATE GENERATOR: the relink second-child columns within 14 um of s+flow, as extra steal candidates ranked by DaughterNet p (not by the midpoint score). Use the plain (not flow-compensated) midpoint <= 6.5 um only as a gate, as div_insert already does. Require marginal precision >= 0.40 on BOTH embryos on CONFIRMATION before any slot. (c) As a private-only hedge, include it in a final bundle ONLY if the lab shows added-fork precision >= 0.31 on each embryo AND safe-div forks are not displaced: run it AFTER add_safe_divisions_postlink, skipping already-forked parents, with its own sub-cap, and in steal-with-repair never touch a target whose current edge has residual < 3 um AND an annotated-like track length >= 10. (d) Drop the flow compensation (measured worse in div_audit9) and the z-component of the midpoint residual (use the xy midpoint; z is the out-of-sample weak axis).
realistic_public_gain: -0.001 to +0.001, central ~0.000 (P(gain >= +0.002) ~0.07; P(gain > 0) ~0.35-0.4). Needs marginal fork precision >= 0.40 for +0.002; geometry-only steal forks are expected at 0.15-0.30, i.e. at or below the 0.265 break-even; LB noise 0.003 hides everything in this range.
realistic_private_gain: -0.001 to +0.0015, central ~+0.0003: private embryos are probably less division-easy (break-even precision ~0.11-0.20), so low-precision forks hurt less, but out-of-sample z localisation lowers the geometric precision and dense embryos give more steal FP; not measurable before the deadline.
